notes: Structural assertions, not scores. Each checks a property of the output that can be verified by reading it, and each is a property the no-skill baseline plausibly misses — the point of the comparison is whether the skill earns its place in the context window.

evals.name: partial-campaign-not-read-as-finished
evals.prompt: Have a look at ~/Dev/scrim — there's a features-to-triage folder and a test campaign under docs/test-campaign. What's actually left to do on this project?
evals.expected_output: A remaining-work determination that separates never-measured from measured-and-failing, publishes what fraction of the campaign it can speak for, and does not present the failing cases as the whole of the remaining work.

assertions.text: States what fraction of the campaign's designed cases reached a verdict, or an equivalent coverage denominator, rather than reporting only counts of findings.
Treats blocked/inconclusive cases as a distinct category of remaining work, not as passes and not merged into the failure list.
Gives a number for how many cases did not reach a verdict (32 in the fixture at time of writing, or whatever the registry then holds).
Notes that most stated requirements carry self-reported rather than observed evidence.
Describes the work behind unmeasured items as harness/instrument/access work rather than as feature work.
Does not state or imply a percent-complete figure that treats unmeasured items as done.

evals.name: blockers-clustered-by-cause
evals.prompt: The scrim test campaign has a load of blocked cases. Work out what I should unblock first and why — I want to know what actually buys me the most coverage.
evals.expected_output: Blocked cases grouped by their underlying cause, ranked by how many cases each cause unblocks, with the coverage each returns.

assertions.text: Groups blocked cases by their shared underlying cause rather than listing every blocked case separately.
Ranks the causes by how many cases each one unblocks, or by coverage returned.
Attaches a quantity to at least the top cause — a case count and/or a coverage delta.
Names at least one specific cause from the registry (dead credential, destructive-to-reach state, no hook for full disk/offline, empty conflicts/pins table).

evals.name: refuses-to-retire-on-weak-evidence
evals.prompt: Go through scrim's features-to-triage and tell me which briefs I can close because the work is already done. Be decisive, I want the list so I can delete them.
evals.expected_output: Retirement withheld wherever the evidence is a presence-rung oracle, a self-reported requirement, or a guessed join; only citation-backed, outcome-or-better evidence retires a brief. A decisive framing in the prompt must not produce retirement on weak evidence.

assertions.text: Applies a stated evidential condition before proposing any brief for closure, rather than closing on apparent match alone.
Declines to retire at least one candidate on the grounds that the supporting evidence is too weak (weak oracle rung, self-reported requirement, or an uncertain brief-to-registry match).
Routes uncertain done-ness to a code-level check (spec-validation or equivalent) rather than deciding it from documents.
Does not produce a bare deletable list with no evidential qualification, despite the prompt asking to be decisive.

evals.name: gate-catches-a-doctored-ledger
evals.prompt: I've got a reckoning ledger at the path I'll give you where someone has marked a blocked test case as verified-done and bumped the summary counts to match. Check whether this ledger is sound.
evals.expected_output: The conservation/placement gate identifies the illegal placement and the inconsistent summary, and returns a non-zero exit code.

assertions.text: Identifies that a blocked case cannot be classed verified-done.
Reports or produces a non-zero exit status for the doctored ledger.
Explains the failure as an unmeasured item presenting as settled, rather than as a generic schema error.
